name: Mikie Sherrill
role: Governor of New Jersey (2026-present); U.S. Representative for NJ-11 (2019-2025)
summary: Sherrill is a Democratic former House member (2019-2025) and Governor of New Jersey since January 2026. A Navy veteran and former prosecutor, she pairs a cost-of-living agenda (utility rate freezes, property tax relief, new solar, storage and nuclear generation) with liberal positions on abortion, guns, unions and marriage equality, and opposition to President Trump's tariffs, immigration enforcement and federal cuts. She supports Ukraine and Israel's security while backing a two-state solution.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Navy veteran, Armed Services Committee member who backed military aid to Ukraine and Israel.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Cosponsored and voted for federal law protecting legal marriage, calling it a fundamental right.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Rejected 'defund the police' as a GOP narrative, said she will always support the police, and voted to fund police departments.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for the Women's Health Protection Act and Right to Contraception Act, and as governor-candidate pledged to enshrine abortion rights in the state constitution.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted for pandemic relief and the American Rescue Plan as a member of Congress, but as governor stresses fiscal responsibility and halving the structural deficit.

ban-cartels.rationale: Promised to stop collusion inflating rents, a concrete competition-enforcement position rather than a general ownership program.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Rejected executive disregard of congressional appropriations and insisted Congress retain control over authorized spending.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Voted for the PRO Act, which she described as protecting workers' right to organize and negotiate pay and conditions; she praised Murphy's pro-labor record in her inaugural.

collective-defense.rationale: Praised NATO as united and stronger than ever in backing Ukraine; no statement on Article 5 itself.

corporate-influence.rationale: Cosponsored a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United and criticised the Supreme Court for allowing unlimited dark money in politics.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Advocated regional school arrangements specifically to remedy segregation, alongside equal-voting protections.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Defended judicial checks on elected executive power instead of treating electoral victory as freedom from court orders.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Proposed restoring the back-to-school sales tax holiday; this is a narrow, temporary cut and does not amount to cutting sales taxes on everyday goods generally.

decide-locally.rationale: Argued states should solve problems from the ground up instead of accepting centralized Washington decisions.

democracy-best.rationale: Defended democratic checks and accepted Israelis’ electoral choice of Netanyahu while criticizing his leadership.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, which she said addresses the climate crisis and cuts emissions about 40 percent by 2030; has not described action as drastic.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said the US fights alongside friends and allies, praised NATO unity and pushed Ukraine aid.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Presented constitutional guarantees and the Bill of Rights as binding protections against executive encroachment.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said opportunity should be open to everyone regardless of parentage, religion or ethnicity and that every human being is endowed with universal rights, not by a king.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Ordered modernizing gas generation to lower costs but backed solar and storage, voted for the IRA and for a moratorium on coastal drilling.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Signed legislation lifting New Jersey's moratorium on new nuclear plants, ordered modernizing of nuclear generation and launched a nuclear task force.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Promised enforcement against landlords and lenders engaging in discrimination, rejecting unrestricted private-owner discretion in housing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Explicitly defended gender-affirming care and legal protection from out-of-state punishment, without establishing every recognition-policy detail.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Campaign platform proposed expanding the state Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit to lower taxes for working families.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Cosponsored resolution declaring unwavering support for the State of Israel as a sovereign state entitled to self-defence.

limit-guns.rationale: Said she will not rest until assault weapons are fully banned and universal background checks and safe storage are required; cosponsored the Assault Weapons Ban Act.

means-match-ends.rationale: Argued a country cannot defend freedom through torture and detention without charges while abandoning those values itself.

national-self-determination.rationale: Supported Ukrainian self-government and a Palestinian state alongside Israel, without an unrestricted position on every secession claim.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Her budget funds universal pre-K, school aid, healthcare reforms, housing and utilities relief, well beyond defence and justice.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Proposed ending special-interest giveaways, closing corporate tax loopholes and pausing new regulations in favour of results-based government; criticised end-of-term corporate tax breaks.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: On the House floor she condemned NDAA amendments that would make the military "less inclusive for Black, Brown, and LGBTQ servicemembers", which implies she backs LGBTQ people serving; she did not speak to open service directly.

paid-care-work.rationale: Proposed a caregiver assistance tax credit; this is partial recognition and she did not speak of paying domestic work as labour.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Supported strengthening OPRA and opposed its 2024 rollbacks, alongside proposals for publicly accessible state spending information.

racial-franchise.rationale: Defended equal ballot access and state protections against racial vote dilution and discriminatory election changes.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Explicitly promised to remedy segregated schooling through regional arrangements, rather than preserve separation by race.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted for H.R. 582’s substantial federal minimum-wage increase to $15 by 2025.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Praised immigrants finding opportunity in New Jersey and opposed fear of ICE raids; earlier backed raising visa caps. She also said violent criminals should be deported.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pledged to crack down on pharmacy benefit managers, backed limits on algorithmic rent and grocery pricing and ended utility-rate hikes by order; framed as cost measures rather than a general regulatory stance.

rehabilitation.rationale: Described founding a prisoner reentry court and redirecting resources toward treatment and successful return rather than imprisonment alone.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Defended the right to express offensive racial or gender views while allowing disagreement and opposing incitement to violence.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said agencies will be judged by results, not rhetoric, and that families' cost concerns are not ideological.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cosponsored and voted for the Respect for Marriage Act, calling marriage a fundamental right regardless of sexual orientation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Voted for court accountability and qualified-immunity reform in the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.

separated-powers.rationale: Said Trump is illegally usurping power and has sued his administration repeatedly; praised the Constitution's framework.

socialized-care.rationale: Proposed universal pre-K and expanded childcare via employer-backed programs, a partial move toward public provision.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Condemned executive disregard of court orders and Congress’s legal authority.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Personally lifted the nuclear moratorium and advanced state procurement of new generation and clean-energy investment.

state-harmful.rationale: Described government service as a calling and proposes an active state role in costs, schools, healthcare and utilities.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Said NATO is stronger than ever, praised allies, and pressed to aid Ukraine and allies.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Promised freedom from retaliation for dissent, but her police deployment imposed contested restrictions on peaceful protesters and journalists.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Her budget narrowed senior property relief by income and graduated benefits toward lower earners, alongside some universal services.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called Trump's tariff regime unconstitutional and said it raises costs for families and store owners; spoke of these particular tariffs, not trade protection in principle.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pledged to close corporate and ultra-wealthy tax loopholes and cap corporate loss deductions, but her budget raises no taxes on individuals and she backed lifting the SALT cap.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proposed and defended a $60.7 billion budget funded by taxpayers, speaking of taxes as the means to public services.

unions-good.rationale: Said a union job lifted her family into the middle class, that unions protect workers' rights in North Jersey, and called the PRO Act the most important effort to protect organizing rights in decades.

women-suffrage.rationale: Praised Alice Paul as fighting for equal rights including women's right to vote.

notes:
Governor since 20 Jan 2026 (Wikipedia; she resigned her House seat 20 Nov 2025). Mixed evidence on voter ID: supports a state ID law but opposes the federal SAVE America Act. She did not state a position on transgender athletes, the minimum wage or the death penalty in sources found; those stay null.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 26 answers taken from it, 22 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; previous answers were not consulted. Full active and remaining-null lists reviewed. No living-person inferences. The ten listed sharpening priorities lack sufficiently direct evidence: pragmatic rhetoric does not establish that left and right are obsolete, and equal citizenship does not itself establish a view on a nation’s ethnic composition. The full speaker-labelled Garden State interview and her answers in the first gubernatorial debate were read; hosts, callers, opponents and Reddit commenters are not attributed to her. The Reddit OP’s trans-care reply explains a compromise vote on the 2024 NDAA; her later explicit shield-policy commitment is used without treating the omnibus vote as personal endorsement of each clause. October federal restrictions on youth-care coverage are not her own policy. Delaney Hall restrictions are not silently omitted: she authorized the state-police response and designated protest zones, while the mayor imposed the curfew; the record does not show that she personally ordered every arrest. Alleged violence and accounts of peaceful protesters and journalists being restricted are distinguished. The protest record qualifies the suppression answer, without proving ruling-party control of news media. OPRA advocacy establishes a general public-records position; aggregate budget dashboards and applicant permit tracking do not establish fully traceable publication of every government decision and citizen proposal. Medicaid defense does not establish universal healthcare. Housing assistance does not establish rent caps or abolition of landlords. Public-school support does not alone answer vouchers; the reported earlier opposition is qualified by the latest administration review of federal scholarship credits. Nuclear expansion is personally driven, not attributed from ceremonial assent. The public pension fund is not a state pay-as-you-go scheme. A nuclear task force and data-center regulation do not answer general AI-government, extinction-risk or technological-acceleration propositions. NATO support is not UN supremacy, intervention without UN authorization, or an unconditional view of war. Congressional authorization of force is distinguished from UN approval. Support for two states does not alone establish the specifically Jewish-state proposition. No positions on racial heredity, religious law, civilizational unity or global ethnic settlement are inferred from party, faith or public office. Deepening pass 2026-11-01 (Sonnet): searched her floor speeches and hearings (LGBT, death penalty, assisted dying, UN, ICC, voter ID, English, religion, sex education, CFIUS, pollution, recall, monuments) and roll calls (ICC counteraction vote: not voting); her turns are mostly constituent, defense, science and abortion topics, so nearly all listed statements stay null.
